mainTopic: Two questions about the service: does a wrong thought while raking the coals for the קטורת disqualify it, and may הולכה (carrying) be done with the left hand?
overview: This amud continues a series of questions about invalid thoughts (מחשבה) during the קטורת service. The גמרא asks whether a wrong thought while raking the coals (חתיית גחלים) disqualifies the service. The answer depends on whether מכשירי מצוה, the preparation steps, count like the מצוה itself. No proof is found, so the question ends with תיקו. Next, the חכמים ask רב ששת whether הולכה, carrying to the place of service, may be done with the left hand. He answers from the משנה, where the כהן גדול holds the coal pan in his right hand and the spoon of incense in his left. The גמרא asks why he did not bring the simpler proof of the תמיד's right leg, which is carried in the left hand. It answers that carrying the limbs is not essential to the כפרה, while carrying the incense is. So רב ששת's source proves that the left hand is valid even for carrying that the כפרה depends on.

steps.title: Does a wrong thought while raking the coals disqualify the incense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if the כהן had an invalidating thought while raking coals, and frames the question as whether preparation steps count as the מצוה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had an invalidating thought while raking up the coals, what is the law? Are the preparation steps of a מצוה treated like the מצוה itself, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question in a series about invalid thoughts (מחשבה) during the service. This time the thought happened while the כהן was raking up burning coals for the incense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raking coals is not the burning of the קטורת itself; it only gets things ready for it. So the question becomes a general one: do מכשירי מצוה have the same status as the מצוה? If they do, a bad thought during the raking would ruin the service, and if not, the thought means nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He had a thought (an invalidating intention, like doing the service for the wrong time or place)
Raking or scooping up the burning coals
Preparation steps that make the מצוה possible

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מכשירי מצוה, whether preparing for a מצוה counts as part of it, comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: If he thought [an invalidating thought] during the raking of the coals, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מַכְשִׁירֵי מִצְוָה כְּמִצְוָה דָּמוּ, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Are the preparations of a מצוה considered like the מצוה itself, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier series of questions on the daf about invalidating thoughts during different stages of the incense service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an invalidating thought during a preparation stage (raking coals) disqualifies the service, which depends on whether מכשירי מצוה count as the מצוה.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle the question and leaves it as תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: No proof is found either way, so the גמרא closes the question with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו does not mean either side is wrong. It means the question stays open. The status of מכשירי מצוה in this case is left undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו is not a ruling that the thought is harmless. It only means the גמרא did not reach an answer.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 1 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether מכשירי מצוה are like the מצוה, and so whether a bad thought during raking coals disqualifies, remains undecided.

steps.title: May carrying be done with the left hand?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב ששת whether הולכה (carrying to the altar) is valid when done with the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: carrying with the left hand, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, this time put to רב ששת. Is it acceptable to carry part of the service with the left hand?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Main parts of the service, like receiving and sprinkling blood, must be done with the right hand. The question is whether הולכה, bringing the item to the altar, also needs the right hand or whether the left is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the offering (or blood or incense) to its place of service

phrases.english: Carrying with the left hand, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about which hand must be used for the service.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הולכה stage of the service is valid if performed with the left hand.

steps.title: רב ששת proves from our משנה that the left hand is fine
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from the משנה: the כהן גדול held the coal pan in his right hand and the spoon of incense in his left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned it. He took the coal pan in his right hand and the spoon in his left hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת says the answer is already in the משנה about the כהן גדול on יום כיפור. The משנה describes him carrying the spoon of incense in his left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול carries the spoon of קטורת into the קודש הקדשים in his left hand, and the service is valid. So carrying with the left hand is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a משנה)
Coal pan (fire pan holding the burning coals)
Spoon or ladle holding the incense

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that הולכה may be done with the left hand.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You have learned it:
He took the coal pan in his right hand
and the spoon in his left hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 using a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Carrying with the left hand is valid, as shown by the כהן גדול carrying the incense spoon in his left hand.

steps.title: Why not prove it from the limbs of the תמיד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ששת did not bring the simpler proof from the משנה where the right leg of the תמיד is carried in the left hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us resolve it for them from what we learned: the right leg was carried in the left hand, with its skin side facing outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to another משנה, about the כהנים carrying the limbs of the קרבן תמיד, that seems to answer the question more directly. Why did רב ששת not use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה clearly shows a כהן carrying a limb in his left hand. If that were enough proof, רב ששת's use of the יום כיפור משנה would seem unnecessary. The challenge pushes us to find what his proof adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The skin side of the limb

phrases.english: And let us resolve it for them from that which we learned:
The right leg [was carried] in the left hand
with its skin side facing outward!
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about carrying the limbs of the תמיד to the ramp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why רב ששת chose his source when a seemingly simpler one exists.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's choice of the יום כיפור incense משנה as his proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about the תמיד limbs already shows carrying in the left hand, so why not use that?

steps.title: The limbs are a weaker case; the incense proof teaches more
steps.stepSummary: From the limbs one could only learn that the left hand is fine when carrying is not essential to the כפרה. רב ששת's source shows it is fine even when carrying is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: If from there, I would have said: that is only carrying that does not hold back atonement, but carrying that does hold back atonement, no. So he teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the limbs משנה would not have been enough proof. It explains why רב ששת needed the incense משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כפרה of a קרבן comes through the blood, so even if the limbs are never carried to the altar the offering still works. That is carrying that is not מעכב the כפרה. The incense on יום כיפור, though, must be brought in for the service to work. Since the left hand is valid there too, it is valid even for essential carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
These words apply (only to this case)
Holds back the atonement; is essential for it

steps.whatToRemember: הולכה with the left hand is valid even when the carrying is essential to the כפרה, as we learn from the כהן גדול carrying the incense spoon in his left hand.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern in the גמרא: a source is chosen because it proves the hardest case, which covers the easier ones too.

phrases.english: If [we learned it] from there, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הוֹלָכָה דְּלָא מְעַכְּבָא כַּפָּרָה,
phrases.english: This applies only to carrying that does not prevent atonement,
but carrying that does prevent atonement — no,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by showing that the limbs source is too weak.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the limbs alone, one would think the left hand is valid only for carrying that is not essential to כפרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The incense משנה proves the left hand is valid even for carrying that is essential to כפרה.
